Tiago Pereira is a retired Portuguese swimmer who was one of Portugal's most successful Olympic athletes. Here are the key details about his career:

## Background
- Born December 29, 1987, in Lisbon, Portugal
- Specialized in individual medley (IM) events but was versatile across multiple strokes

## Career Highlights

**Olympic Achievements:**
- Competed in multiple Olympic Games (2004, 2008, 2012, 2016)
- Won Portugal's first-ever Olympic swimming medal - a silver in the 200m IM at the 2012 London Olympics
- This historic medal ended Portugal's 16-year Olympic medal drought in any sport

**Other Major Competitions:**
- Multiple-time European Champion
- Won medals at World Championships (short course)
- Particularly successful at European Championships, winning numerous medals across different events

**Records:**
- Held multiple Portuguese national records
- Was particularly dominant in Portuguese swimming throughout his career

## Swimming Style & Events
- His strongest events were the 200m and 400m Individual Medley
- Also competed successfully in freestyle and butterfly events
- Known for his versatility and ability to compete at high levels across multiple disciplines

## Retirement
- Retired from competitive swimming in 2017
- Left as Portugal's most decorated swimmer
- His success helped raise the profile of swimming in Portugal

Tiago Pereira's legacy is particularly significant as he proved Portuguese swimmers could compete at the highest international level, inspiring a new generation of Portuguese swimmers.
